doc.title: Putter Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 27, 2024

title: The 1987 Oleo video with Ed Thigpen, and Chubby Jackson on playing without amps
summary: Rowe cites a video of Smith, Ed Thigpen and Ron Eschete playing Oleo at 320 bpm. They discuss the physical strain of bass, quoting Chubby Jackson.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Play for your supper. I mentioned Jimmy Wormworth because he’s from Utica where I am, and he is a well known local figure. I found on the internet the video, and I wonder if you remember this, it came from 1987 from the Guitar Institute and you’re playing with Ed Thigpen and Ron — a guitar player Ron?

Eschete. And you’re playing “Oleo.” And this thing was so fast that I got out an on-line metronome and I tried to figure out the tempo. And it’s so fast that it was off the chart. And I had to figure out okay what are the beats per minute of the half note. And this thing was like 320 beats per minute. Do you remember this?
Oh yeah. Oh yeah. No I saw that, someone sent that to me in the last couple of years. And I said my God how did I do it? How could I do it?
Well that’s the easy part. It’s going bing-bing-bing-bing-bing-bing that’s the hard part. You know. Ed Thigpen, a great drummer.
Yeah. I was stunned by that. I had a quote here from Chubby Jackson. And we were talking about, you know as a bass player we were talking about that. And he said — I

thought of him back then watching Woody Herman’s band with the lack of amplification and he said, “A lot of times your arms and fingers get numb. You’re playing — you start to shake physically at the moment, and then someone looks at you and says ‘take one’ the laugh of the century, somebody points to the bass player after 28 choruses, your hands are like this. My hands were so ugly I used to keep them in my pocket all the time.”

Yeah. Absolutely. And he was playing without an amp. And he was a very good bass player. His son was out here for a while, Duffy. Very good drummer. Very good drummer. I think he ended up in Miami. But Chubby was a very good bass player.
